Host policy stays outside this family: Hub admits funded slots, standalone
admits its current owner. Both call their durable fleet through this port. Keep
the host contract independent of the Worker-only fleet lifecycle.

### OysterCallerAccess

```ts
type OysterCallerAccess =
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "agent";
      policy: AppToolPolicy;
    }>
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "key";
      keyId: string;
      byInstallation: ReadonlyMap<string, AppToolPolicy>;
    }>
  | null;
```

The App-tool access one caller's catalog capture used, re-checked at call time
against a fresh read. An Agent's policy is one blanket level for every
installation (`host.appToolPolicy`); a key's is its own grants, resolved per
installation (`appToolAccess`) -- an installation the key has no grant for is
captured as absent, never merely refused, so it is never listed at all.

### oysterAppMethods()

```ts
function oysterAppMethods(
  host,
  principal,
  access,
  surfaces,
  preloadedInstallations?,
): Promise<
  Readonly<{
    id: string;
    acquire: (context) => Promise<
      Readonly<{
        snapshot: CapabilitySourceSnapshot;
        release: () => Promise<void>;
      }>
    >;
  }> &
    object
>;
```

Capture installed App methods for MCP or agents as one principal-scoped source.
Enabled installations become `env.<APP>` modules using the Instance call path; a
dotted method such as `repos.list` is `env.<APP>.repos.list()`. Owners see every
discoverable method. A key sees only the installations its own grants admit,
each at the level (`read`/`write`) those grants give it; Mycelium itself refuses
a write call up front when the module's own grant is `read`
(`mycelium/src/access.ts`). Call again to capture changes to Releases,
installation authority or the caller's own grants.

### oysterComputerTools()

```ts
function oysterComputerTools(host, principal): Promise<
  | Readonly<{
  id: string;
  acquire: (context) => Promise<Readonly<{
     snapshot: CapabilitySourceSnapshot;
     release: () => Promise<...>;
  }>>;
}> & object
| null>;
```

Capture the host's fixed Computer for one caller as a Knapsack source. The host
decides whether the caller holds Computer access; the ComputerDO still checks
its host-issued grant on every call. Null when the host has no Computer or the
caller has no access. Grants name the captured module.

### oysterMcpCatalogLoad()

```ts
function oysterMcpCatalogLoad(host): (principal) => Promise<Readonly<{
  instructions: string;
  sources: readonly Readonly<{
     id: string;
     acquire: (context) => Promise<Readonly<{
        snapshot: ...;
        release: ...;
     }>>;
  }>[];
  grants: Grants;
}>>;
```

Load the current catalog for an authenticated owner or key: installed App
methods, plus the host's Computer when the caller holds Computer access. A key
sees exactly the installations and levels its own grants admit, and the Computer
only with its own `computer.use` grant; each App retains its own caller checks
regardless. App writes use the host's approval record; stored approval of an
Agent's App tools can permit headless App writes. The shared MCP server elicits
consent for explicitly confirmed operations, including every advertised
Workspace Computer call, even reads. Each call still re-admits the key, checks
current App approval and passes the App's gate.

#### Parameters

| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`    | `Pick`\<[`OysterHost`](host.md#oysterhost), \| `"installations"` \| `"instances"` \| `"artifacts"` \| `"guestLimits"` \| `"backgroundOriginKey"` \| `"computerId"` \| `"computer"` \| `"computerControl"` \| `"capabilities"` \| `"appToolPolicy"` \| `"keys"` \| `"workflows"`\> |

`Promise`\<`Readonly`\<\{ `snapshot`: ...; `release`: ...; \}\>\>; \}\>[];
`grants`: `Grants`; \}\>\>
